title: Cross-region routing oscillation due to smart-routing policy regression — mitigation and action plan
creator: Priya Shah
description: Summary: On 2026-03-01 a traffic routing regression caused repeated cross-region reroutes and variant churn for a subset of production customers. The oscillation increased p95/p99 latencies, caused elevated 5xx rates for routed pods, and triggered degraded throughput for dedicated capacity pools. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations applied, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-01 02:13 UTC — First alert: spike in reroute_count and upstream 503s for eu-west-1 customers
2026-03-01 02:18 UTC — On-call identified increasing cross-region sticky assignments and concurrent cache flushes
2026-03-01 02:25 UTC — Scoped to smart-routing policy evaluation path after reviewing request traces and route-change frequency
2026-03-01 02:40 UTC — Emergency rollback of routing-policy change (PR #4567) to stop TTL reset behavior
2026-03-01 03:05 UTC — Applied temporary global routing override to lock per-request region decisions for 10 minutes
2026-03-01 04:10 UTC — Capacity autoscaler engaged to absorb transient load; metrics returned to baseline by 06:00 UTC
2026-03-01 09:00 UTC — Post-incident conference call: initial root cause hypothesis and owner assignments
impact: Several customers experienced increased latency and intermittent errors for 1.5–3.5 hours; internal dedicated pools saw reduced effective throughput during the oscillation window. No data loss. Estimated customer sessions affected: low-to-medium number of high-value customers on inter-region failover paths.
root_cause: A regression introduced in PR #4567 changed the fallback TTL computation to be dynamic but returned a null/zero TTL in a race when variant metadata was rehydrated from cache. This caused sticky routing metadata to be cleared on certain responses, which in turn triggered immediate reroute decisions. The combination of per-request TTL resets and simultaneous autoscaling/reassignment produced oscillatory behavior across regions. Additional contributing factors: insufficient integration tests for TTL edge cases and lack of an oscillation detector/circuit-breaker in the routing controller.
mitigations_applied: Rolled back PR #4567 at 02:40 UTC (see PR #4572) to restore previous TTL semantics
Applied a temporary global override to prefer local-region sticky routing for 10 minutes
Disabled aggressive variant fallback for traffic matching enterprise tiers until fix validated
Scaled up dedicated capacity pools to reduce impact while root cause investigated
Added short-term alert threshold on reroute_rate and route-change-per-request to aid on-call
action_items: A1 — Diego Martinez — due 2026-03-18 — Make TTL computation idempotent and ensure it never returns null: add defensive checks and unit tests
A2 — Priya Shah — due 2026-03-22 — Add per-request reroute circuit-breaker: stop more than N reroutes for same request/user within T seconds
A3 — Maria Lopez — due 2026-03-29 — Create an integration test that simulates cache rehydration race and validates sticky metadata survives concurrent variant updates
A4 — Owen Reed — due 2026-03-25 — Instrument additional telemetry: route-change histogram, TTL-assignment source, variant-change causal traces (link to schema in notes)
A5 — SRE Team — due 2026-03-15 — Add Grafana dashboard panel & alert for reroute oscillation (reroutes/sec + unique-request reroute frequency)
A6 — QA — due 2026-04-01 — Run cross-region chaos test (controlled) against staging with simulated fallback conditions and autoscaler load
A7 — Product — due 2026-03-28 — Document expected fallback semantics in Smart Routing runbook and update rollback playbook
notes: Root cause trace: variant-metadata TTL path had a null-return branch introduced in PR #4567 (line changed in router/policy_eval.go)
Regression slipped through because unit tests only covered positive TTL values; no negative/null tests existed
Customer comms coordinated with support and account teams; targeted outreach to affected customers completed 2026-03-02
